messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Oveflow of an (indirectly) constrained parameter
parts:
Hello,

I have been working on my model of a "mood" conditioned LDA (for bioinformatics). Here I fix beta (superparameter of phi, distribution of words in topics) as linear function, where Y axes (beta) is a value of prevalence of a word and x axes is "mood" (sigma<lower=1, upper=2>). While beta and sigma are parameters I have the coefficients c and a of the equations: [beta = sigma * a + c]

I understood (I think) how to model this linear function, but now I am getting an error that I should not get in my mind.

Exception thrown at line 32: Error in function boost::math::lgamma<double>(double): numeric overflow    23

since the x (sigma) is constrained [1,2] I know that all my functions within 1-2 get normal values of y (beta), not of course infinite.

I provide my R script, please copy&paste to reproduce error
=============================================
K <-
4L
W <-
5L
M <-
4L
N <-
20L
w <-
c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 
1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L)
w_count <-
c(1171L, 83L, 1300L, 422L, 180L, 49L, 17L, 436L, 129L, 150L, 
754L, 56L, 1339L, 349L, 262L, 87L, 22L, 717L, 97L, 128L)
tot_w_count <-
1339L
doc <-
c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L)
alpha <-
c(1, 1, 1, 1)
c <-
structure(c(10481.2, 341.027, 1216.76, 275.06, 1153.071, 15.107, 
15.856, 19.814, 9802.11, 1453.75, 1517.97, 1059.2, 3198.48, 216.367, 
401.72, 162.948, 2568.14, -103.87, -10.848, -74.112), .Dim = 4:5, .Dimnames = list(
    NULL, NULL), class = c("cast_matrix", "matrix"))
a <-
structure(c(-5188.3, -149.737, -545.43, -40.8399999999999, -547.971, 
4.175, 3.22, 2.78, -4588.21, -593.33, -477.07, -114.66, -1487.88, 
-68.537, -82.6799999999999, -44.038, -1160.34, 123.48, 61.614, 
91.106), .Dim = 4:5, .Dimnames = list(NULL, NULL), class = c("cast_matrix", 
"matrix"))

myM <- "
data {
  int<lower=2> K;               // num topics
  int<lower=2> W;               // num words
  int<lower=1> M;               // num docs
  int<lower=1> N;               // total word instances
  int<lower=0> tot_w_count;     //upper value for word counts
  vector<lower=0, upper=tot_w_count>[N] w_count;   // word count per document (e.g., cat in document 1 is present 5 times)
  int<lower=1,upper=W> w[N];    // word n
  int<lower=1,upper=M> doc[N];  // doc ID for word n
  vector<lower=0>[K] alpha;     // topic prior
  
  matrix[K, W] c;
  matrix[K, W] a;
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta[M];   // topic dist for doc m   
  real<lower=0> beta[K,W];     // words prior
  simplex[W] phi[M,K];
  vector<lower=1,upper=2>[M] sigma; //mood
} 
model {
  for (m in 1:M) {
    theta[m] ~ dirichlet(alpha);  // prior     
    for(k in 1:K) {
      beta[k] ~ normal(c[k] + a[k] * sigma[m], 0.0001);       
      phi[m,k] ~ dirichlet(to_vector(beta[k]));
    } 
  }
  for (n in 1:N) {    
    real gamma[K];    
    for (k in 1:K) gamma[k] <- log(theta[doc[n],k]) + log(phi[doc[n],k, w[n]]);
    if(w_count[n]>0) increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(gamma) * w_count[n]);  // likelihood
  }
}
"

suppressMessages(library(rstan))
my.in <- list(K = K,W = W,M = M,N = N,w = w, w_count = w_count, tot_w_count = tot_w_count, doc = doc,alpha = alpha,c=c, a=a)
fit <- stan(model_code=myM   , data=my.in, chains=1) 
============================================


On beta I don't have up constrains, but according to a, c, sigma[1,2] beta should NEVER get to values that I don;t expect, since those linear functions are regression based on two limit points that seat (surprise, surprise) in 1 and 2.

Thanks for your support!
Stefano

On Monday, December 21, 2015 at 9:30:52 AM UTC+11, Bob Carpenter wrote:
The gamma function has poles at 0 and negative integers.
See:  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_function

I didn't understand the x/sigma thing.  It looks like sigma
is your parameter.

Yes sigma is the "mood" for every document, instead of providing a known multinomial (collection of probabilities) for words in a topic (phi), I provide a collection of linear functions that all depend on one variable "mood" unknown for every document (sigma).

How are a and c constrained in beta = sigma * a + c?  If
they're what you define in that big matrix in the code, they're
unconstrained, and therefore so is beta.

This consideration, that I can't get, makes me think that I am missing something huge.
In my mind, for example, if

1) I set c = 2 and a = 2 for a word in a tipic and
2) use the equation beta = sigma * 2 + 2, and
3) constrain sigma > 1 and < 2 (because the mood can be just between 1 and 2)
4) I should obtain beta with the min-max values of 4 and 6, so if
5) sample from beta ~ normal(c + a * sigma, 0.0001), I should obtain
6) beta with a possible range of ~2, ~4
7) How can beta be overflown

What am I misunderstanding?

P.S. Instead of establishing beta I could establish directly Phi from the linear equations, with the problem of Phi not being a simplex anymore.

Thanks a lot

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Oveflow of an (indirectly) constrained parameter
parts:
There are multiple problems with your model in this
one line:
> beta[k] ~ normal(c[k] + a[k] * sigma[m], 0.0001);

you have constrained sigma[m] in (1, 2), but c[k] and a[k]
are unconstrained. So c[k] + a[k] * sigma[m] is unconstrained.

I'm not sure if you realized that Stan's normal distribution
is parameterized with scale (or standard deviation), not with
precision (1 / std_dev^2). So the above means you're constraining
beta[k] to be very very close to c[k] + a[k] * sigma[m].

- Bob

data {
  int<lower=2> K;               // num topics
  int<lower=2> W;               // num words
  int<lower=1> M;               // num docs
  int<lower=1> N;               // total word instances
  int<lower=0> tot_w_count;     //upper value for word counts
  vector<lower=0, upper=tot_w_count>[N] w_count;   // word count per document (e.g., cat in document 1 is present 5 times)
  int<lower=1,upper=W> w[N];    // word n
  int<lower=1,upper=M> doc[N];  // doc ID for word n
  vector<lower=0>[K] alpha;     // topic prior
simplex[W] phi[K];            // word dist for topic k

}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta[M];   // topic dist for doc m     
}

model {
  for (m in 1:M) theta[m] ~ dirichlet(alpha);  // prior

for (n in 1:N) {
    real gamma[K];
for (k in 1:K) gamma[k] <- (log(theta[doc[n],k]) + log(phi[k,w[n]]));

if(w_count[n]>0) increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(gamma) * w_count[n]);  // likelihood
  }
}

The modification I am trying to work is: if a topic uses different words depending (linear relationship) on the "mood" (sigma) of the writer (one mood per document), how can I identify sigma (mood) and theta (topic proportion per document)?

Again the information I have is all linear relationships [K, W] (instead of having phi). So instead of having one phi, I will have one phi per document. This phi while provided before, now will be a parameter.

data {
  int<lower=2> K;               // num topics
  int<lower=2> W;               // num words
  int<lower=1> M;               // num docs
  int<lower=1> N;               // total word instances
  int<lower=0> tot_w_count;     //upper value for word counts
  vector<lower=0, upper=tot_w_count>[N] w_count;   // word count per document (e.g., cat in document 1 is present 5 times)
  int<lower=1,upper=W> w[N];    // word n
  int<lower=1,upper=M> doc[N];  // doc ID for word n
  vector<lower=0>[K] alpha;     // topic prior
real<lower=0> beta_max; //max value for beta based on my data

matrix[K, W] c;
  matrix[K, W] a;
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta[M];   // topic dist for doc m

real<lower=0, upper=beta_max> beta[M,K,W];     // words prior
  real<lower=0, upper=1> phi[M,K,W];

vector<lower=1,upper=2>[M] sigma; //mood
} 
model {
  for (m in 1:M) {
    theta[m] ~ dirichlet(alpha);  // prior     
    for(k in 1:K) {

beta[m,k] ~ normal(c[k] + a[k] * sigma[m], 0.0001);       
      phi[m,k] ~ dirichlet(to_vector(beta[m,k]));

} 
  }
  for (n in 1:N) {    
    real gamma[K];    
    for (k in 1:K) gamma[k] <- log(theta[doc[n],k]) + log(phi[doc[n],k, w[n]]);
    if(w_count[n]>0) increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(gamma) * w_count[n]);  // likelihood
  }
}

Thanks
 

- Bob
